head.citation-title: Innovative application of SDCM-PHC integrated pile-column system in semi-cover excavation metro stations: Mechanical behavior and performance validation
head.abstracts: © 2025 Elsevier Ltd.Semi-cover excavation is widely adopted in metro station construction, where central columns critically govern structural stability. Conventional steel-concrete composite columns with bored piles necessitate extensive post-construction steel tube cutting, incurring significant time and cost penalties. To address this, we propose an innovative application of stiffened deep cement mixing (SDCM) piles, formed by embedding prefabricated PHC pipe piles into freshly cast deep cement mixing (DCM) piles, within central column systems. This SDCM-PHC integrated system leverages dual-layer load transfer for enhanced bearing capacity while eliminating cutting requirements. Then, mechanical behavior was investigated, including variation of displacement and bending moment during station excavation through field monitoring; structural responses and parametric analysis using finite element modeling. The results show that peak structural demands (axial force, shear force, bending moment) concentrate at column tops, and increasing PHC pile stiffness from 0.5EI to 1.5EI amplifies column-top displacement by 59.09 % and cover slab settlement by 59.71 %. The solution satisfies structural requirements while reducing construction costs, providing valuable references for metro station applications.
